subject: Data residency & bespoke retention windows — SummitHealth order form
messages:
From: Laura Miles <laura.miles@summithealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Compliance Team <compliance@summithealth.com>, Summit Health Procurement <procurement@summithealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency / retention windows question

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the call earlier — quick follow-up from our compliance team. We have two items we need to lock into the order form / SOW before procurement will proceed: 

1) For PHI processed via the Redwood hosted offering, we need a hard retention window on request logs and generated artifacts. Our baseline ask is 90 days, but some teams will need up to 365 days depending on audit needs. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
   - Offer a per-account bespoke retention window (e.g., 90 / 180 / 365 days)
   - Guarantee irreversible deletion after the window with a deletion timestamp in logs

2) Data residency: all customer data must remain in the us-west-2 region (and never be replicated to other regions).

Procurement also asked about the deletion timeline — once a deletion is requested (or retention expires), how long until data is purged and how is that reflected in the audit logs?

Appreciate a short write-up so we can attach it to the SOW.

Best,
Laura
Laura Miles
Senior Compliance Manager, Summit Health

-----

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Miles <laura.miles@summithealth.com>
Cc: Prioyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Compliance Team <compliance@summithealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency / retention windows question

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. High level: yes, we can support per-account bespoke retention windows and region-locking to us-west-2 for hosted deployments. Below is the operational summary we propose for insertion into the SOW / order form (short, so procurement can review quickly):

- Retention windows: Redwood will support configurable retention windows per account for request logs and generated artifacts with granular options: 90 / 180 / 365 days (customer selects at onboarding). Custom retention >365 days can be accommodated via Dedicated or Private deployment with a separate commercial term.

- Deletion guarantees: At retention expiry or on customer-initiated deletion, Redwood will schedule permanent deletion of the retained artifacts and request logs. Deletion process: immediate logical deletion (removal from live indexes/cache) within 24 hours; physical crypto-shredding of backups and object-store lifecycle enforcement completed within 30 days. A deletion event is recorded to the account's audit log with UTC timestamp and a deletion_event_id.

- Data residency: For Summit Health, all data and backups will be pinned to us-west-2. No cross-region replication will occur without explicit written consent.

- Auditability: Audit logs will include retention_window (days), deletion_event_id, deletion_request_ts, and deletion_completion_ts. Logs are retained per the selected retention window plus 30 days for compliance traceability (this is to ensure we can provide proof-of-deletion within a predictable window). For extended log retention we can add a separate logging-addendum.

I'll attach a draft SOW excerpt and a diagram of the deletion workflow. If that looks good, Marissa can confirm legal language for the order form.

Attachment: redwood-data-deletion-flow.png (image/png)

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Prioyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Miles <laura.miles@summithealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency / retention windows question

Laura — quick technical clarifications from my side to make sure the SOW language maps to runtime behavior: 

- "Immediate logical deletion (within 24 hours)": this means evidence of deletion (removed from active indices and caches) is observable within 24h and a deletion_event_id appears in audit logs. However, ephemeral inference caches (KV caches) may have shorter TTLs and are not treated as durable logs.

- "Crypto-shredding of backups within 30 days": our standard backup lifecycle and blob-store policies use object-store lifecycle rules plus key-rotation-aware crypto-shredding. For the hosted offering in us-west-2 we can guarantee crypto-shredding within 30 days of deletion request/expiry. If Summit Health requires a shorter guaranteed purging window (e.g., 7 days), we recommend Dedicated where we can commit to accelerated deletion SLAs (commercial impact applies).

- Attachments: redwood-data-deletion-flow.png shows the stepwise events (deletion_request -> logical_removal -> backup_lifecycle -> crypto_shred -> audit_finalized).

Happy to hop on a 20-minute tech call if you want to walk the diagram with engineering.

— Prioyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

-----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Miles <laura.miles@summithealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Prioyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency / retention windows question

Laura — legal here. I reviewed Jordan and Prioyom's proposed language and we can proceed with the following order form clause for Summit Health: 

1) Retention options: Customer will elect a retention window for request logs and generated artifacts at onboarding: 90 / 180 / 365 days. Election is captured in the Order Form. Requests for retention windows longer than 365 days must be executed under Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private and will be the subject of a separate addendum.

2) Deletion and proof: Upon expiry or customer-requested deletion, Redwood will: 
   a. Perform logical removal within 24 hours (removal from primary indexes and inference caches). 
   b. Initiate object-store lifecycle actions and crypto-shredding of backups; completion target: within 30 calendar days. 
   c. Provide an auditable deletion_event_id and deletion_completion_ts in the account's audit log.

3) Residency: All customer data will be processed and stored in AWS us-west-2 and will not be replicated outside the region without prior written consent.

We will include the short excerpt above in the SOW and push the updated document for signature. Jordan — please send final SOW to procurement. Laura — attaching a DocuSign envelope for the order form once you confirm.
